does: Works flour, yeast, yogurt, milk and a little oil into a soft, slightly sticky dough, then leaves it covered to rise until it is puffy and light. The yogurt and the yeast together make a dough that stays soft and chewy once it is cooked on a hot plate.

intro.what: This naan dough combines yeast, yogurt and milk into a soft dough that rises before shaping.
intro.why: It teaches you to recognise a light, slightly tacky dough without drying it through excess flour.

how: Stir the yeast and the sugar into the warm milk and leave them until the top turns foamy.
Mix the flour and the salt in a large bowl, make a well, and pour in the yeast milk, the yogurt and the oil.
Work it together into a rough dough, then knead on a floured board until it is smooth, soft and only a little sticky.
Put the dough in an oiled bowl, turn it once to coat it, and cover it.
Leave it in a warm place until it has swelled and feels light and springy.

cues.text: The dough has swelled well past its first size and the surface is smooth and domed.
It is soft and a little tacky, and springs back slowly when pressed with a finger.

mistakes.mistake: Adding much more flour to stop the stickiness, which gives a dry, tough bread.
mistakes.fix: Keep the dough soft and use only a dusting of flour on the board.

mistakes.mistake: Pouring hot milk onto the yeast, which kills it so the dough never rises.
mistakes.fix: Use milk that is only comfortably warm to a finger.

mistakes.mistake: Leaving the dough uncovered, so that a dry skin forms.
mistakes.fix: Cover the bowl with a damp cloth or a plate.

quiz.question: What dough texture supports the soft, chewy naan in this method?
choices: Dry and stiff without any tackiness.
Loose enough to pour like batter.
quiz.because: A soft slightly tacky dough gives this bread its intended texture; excess flour makes it dry.

quiz.question: How should the bowl be kept while the dough rises?
choices: Open and heavily dusted until a skin forms.
quiz.because: Covering keeps the surface from drying as the dough rises.

quiz.question: Which change shows the dough has risen?
choices: It stays dense at the starting size.
A dry hard crust forms on top.
It swells and feels light and springy.
quiz.because: Swelling and a light springy feel accompany the rise, rather than a dry skin.

quiz.question: Extra flour has made the dough dry and the bread tough. What would you change next time?
choices: Keep the dough soft and dust the board only lightly.
Work in flour until all tackiness disappears.
Leave the dough uncovered to firm it further.
quiz.because: A little tackiness is expected; too much added flour makes the bread dry and tough.

variant_of.differs: The dough is leavened with yeast and enriched with yogurt, milk and oil, so it is softer and stickier, kneaded briefly and left to rise before it is cooked.
